name: Box64: 64 KiB guard reservation at 0xffff0000 to stop guest allocations rolling over the 32-bit boundary
required_postconditions: the last 64 KiB below 2^32 is occupied by Box64 itself so no guest object can be placed there
the mapping is requested WITHOUT MAP_FIXED: the kernel is only hinted, and the code tests cur == (void*)(0x100000000LL-65536) afterwards
if the hint is not honoured the guard does not exist and guest pointer arithmetic near 0xffffffff can wrap

failure_sink.description: if the mapping lands anywhere else the code logs ' Tried to reserve high %p+>%p' at LOG_INFO, unmaps it and returns. Nothing is retried and no caller is told. The stated purpose - 'to avoid roll over on some opcodes' - is then simply not achieved, silently.

source_locations.symbol: comment: '// reserve area close to 0xffffffff too, to avoid roll over on some opcodes...'
InternalMmap((void*)(0x100000000LL-65536), 65536, 0, MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0) - note prot=0 and no MAP_FIXED
if(cur!=MAP_FAILED && (cur==(void*)(0x100000000LL-65536))) - exactness is tested, not enforced
rb_set(mapallmem, cur, cur+65536, MEM_RESERVED) - only on the exact-address path

extraction_limitations: the source expresses the address as the arithmetic 0x100000000LL-65536 rather than a literal 0xffff0000.

x_campaign.rationale: The address is free on a normal x86-64 Linux process so the hint is usually honoured, but the request carries no MAP_FIXED and the probe measured hinted_mapping_may_relocate=true, so exact placement is not guaranteed.
